drugs.boxed_warning: Antidepressants increased the risk compared to placebo of suicidal thinking and behavior (suicidality) in children, adolescents, and young adults in short-term studies of major depressive disorder (MDD) and other psychiatric disorders.
drugs.dosage_and_administration: Initial dose one tablet (15 mg) three times a day; increase to at least 60 mg/day at a fairly rapid pace consistent with patient tolerance, up to 90 mg daily. Maintenance may be reduced slowly to as low as 15 mg daily or every other day.
drugs.warnings_and_cautions: Avoid foods with high tyramine content including aged cheeses, pickled herring, cured meats, fermented products, and fava bean pods; restrict caffeine and chocolate. These foods may cause a reaction characterized by headache and other serious symptoms due to a rise in blood pressure (hypertensive crisis).
drugs.food_effect: Tyramine-containing foods must be restricted; ingestion during therapy can precipitate hypertensive crisis. This is a dietary-interaction restriction, not an absorption effect.
drugs.drug_interactions: Do not combine with serotonergic agents (fluoxetine, sertraline, paroxetine), meperidine, sympathomimetics, other MAO inhibitors, buspirone, dextromethorphan, CNS depressants, or bupropion. At least 14 days should elapse between discontinuation of phenelzine and initiation of most other antidepressants; five weeks for fluoxetine.
drugs.common_adverse_reactions: Dizziness, headache, drowsiness, insomnia, fatigue, weakness, tremors, constipation, dry mouth, weight gain, postural hypotension, and sexual disturbances.

drugs.boxed_warning: WARNING: SUICIDAL THOUGHTS AND BEHAVIORS and HYPERTENSIVE CRISIS WITH SIGNIFICANT TYRAMINE USE.
drugs.dosage_and_administration: Starting dose 30 mg daily in divided doses; may increase by 10 mg every 1 to 3 weeks to a maximum of 60 mg daily. Elderly patients require more gradual increases due to hypotension risk. Discontinue gradually.
drugs.warnings_and_cautions: Restrict tyramine intake during treatment and for 2 weeks after stopping. Avoid aged cheeses, cured/fermented meats, pickled herring, fava beans, sauerkraut, concentrated yeast extract, most soy products, tap/unpasteurized beers, and spoiled or improperly stored foods. Risk of hypertensive crisis.
drugs.food_effect: Foods high in tyramine can precipitate hypertensive crisis; safe alternatives include fresh meats, processed cheeses, most vegetables, and bottled/canned beer.
drugs.drug_interactions: Contraindicated with SSRIs, SNRIs, tricyclic antidepressants, other MAOIs, sympathomimetics (pseudoephedrine, phenylephrine), triptans, meperidine, tramadol, buspirone, dextromethorphan, carbamazepine, tryptophan, and SAM-e, due to risk of hypertensive crisis or serotonin syndrome.
drugs.common_adverse_reactions: Most frequent (>30%): dry mouth, dizziness, insomnia, sedation, headache. Also common (>10%): overexcitement, constipation, blurred vision, tremor.

drugs.boxed_warning: Lithium toxicity is closely related to serum lithium concentrations, and can occur at doses close to therapeutic concentrations.
drugs.dosage_and_administration: Adults and pediatric patients over 30 kg: start 300 mg three times daily. Pediatric patients 20 to 30 kg: start 300 mg twice daily. Target serum concentrations 0.8 to 1.2 mEq/L for acute treatment and 0.8 to 1.0 mEq/L for maintenance.
drugs.warnings_and_cautions: Patients should maintain a normal diet, including salt, and an adequate fluid intake (2,500 to 3,000 mL). Dehydration increases toxicity risk. Risk factors for toxicity include volume depletion or dehydration, recent onset of concurrent febrile illness, and impaired renal function.
drugs.food_effect: No absorption-based food effect specified; the clinically relevant dietary factors are consistent sodium intake and adequate fluid intake (2,500 to 3,000 mL).
drugs.drug_interactions: Diuretics, NSAIDs, renin-angiotensin antagonists, and nitroimidazoles increase lithium levels. Serotonergic drugs carry a risk of serotonin syndrome. Antipsychotics combined with lithium may cause an encephalopathic syndrome.
drugs.common_adverse_reactions: Adults: fine hand tremor, polyuria, mild thirst, nausea, general discomfort. Pediatric (7-17 years): nausea/vomiting, polyuria, thyroid abnormalities, tremor, thirst, dizziness, rash, ataxia, decreased appetite, blurry vision.

drugs.boxed_warning: WARNING: INCREASED MORTALITY IN ELDERLY PATIENTS WITH DEMENTIA-RELATED PSYCHOSIS. Elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis treated with antipsychotic drugs are at an increased risk of death.
drugs.dosage_and_administration: Administer orally with food. Capsules should be swallowed whole and not opened, crushed, or chewed.
drugs.warnings_and_cautions: Somnolence is common (14% in schizophrenia trials, 31% in bipolar mania trials); caution with activities requiring alertness. QT prolongation risk limits combination with other QT-prolonging drugs.
drugs.food_effect: The absorption of ziprasidone is increased up to two-fold in the presence of food; absolute bioavailability is approximately 60% when taken with a meal.
drugs.drug_interactions: Ziprasidone should not be used in combination with other drugs that have demonstrated QT prolongation. Serotonin syndrome risk exists with concomitant serotonergic medications.
drugs.common_adverse_reactions: Schizophrenia: somnolence (14%), respiratory tract infection (8%). Bipolar mania/mixed: somnolence (31%), extrapyramidal symptoms (31%), dizziness (16%).

drugs.boxed_warning: Elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis treated with antipsychotic drugs are at an increased risk of death. Olanzapine is not approved for the treatment of patients with dementia-related psychosis.
drugs.dosage_and_administration: Administer orally once daily without regard to meals. Schizophrenia (adults): start 5 to 10 mg daily, target 10 mg/day within several days. Bipolar I (adults): start 10 to 15 mg daily. Adolescents 13-17: start 2.5 to 5 mg, target 10 mg/day. Reduced starting dose (5 mg) for debilitated patients or those predisposed to hypotension or slowed metabolism.
drugs.warnings_and_cautions: Metabolic changes: hyperglycemia (mean fasting glucose increase 2.76 mg/dL vs 0.17 mg/dL placebo), dyslipidemia with significant triglyceride elevations, and weight gain (adults gained a mean 2.6 kg vs 0.3 kg loss on placebo; 22.2% gained at least 7% of baseline weight; adolescents mean 4.6 kg increase). Monitor glucose and lipids at baseline and periodically.
drugs.food_effect: Olanzapine may be administered without regard to meals; food does not meaningfully affect absorption.
drugs.drug_interactions: When combining with fluoxetine and lithium or valproate, consult the respective package inserts. Anticholinergic medications increase the risk of severe adverse reactions.
drugs.common_adverse_reactions: Somnolence (26% vs 15% placebo), orthostatic hypotension, weight gain, constipation, dry mouth, tachycardia, and prolactin elevation.

drugs.boxed_warning: WARNING: SEVERE NEUTROPENIA; ORTHOSTATIC HYPOTENSION, BRADYCARDIA, AND SYNCOPE; SEIZURE; MYOCARDITIS, PERICARDITIS, AND CARDIOMYOPATHY; INCREASED MORTALITY IN ELDERLY PATIENTS WITH DEMENTIA-RELATED PSYCHOSIS.
drugs.dosage_and_administration: Starting dose is 12.5 mg once or twice daily, titrating to 150 mg to 225 mg twice per day by the end of two weeks, with a maximum of 450 mg twice daily. Orally disintegrating tablets may be chewed or allowed to disintegrate without water.
drugs.warnings_and_cautions: Associated with hyperglycemia, dyslipidemia, and significant weight gain: 35% of clozapine patients experienced weight gain of at least 7% of baseline body weight versus 8% on chlorpromazine; mean triglyceride increase of +71 mg/dL (54%). Sedation is common.
drugs.drug_interactions: For strong CYP1A2 inhibitors, administer one third of the usual clozapine dosage. Moderate or weak CYP1A2 or CYP3A4 inducers may require dosage increases. Strong CYP3A4 inducers are not recommended; if necessary, increase dosage and monitor effectiveness.
drugs.common_adverse_reactions: Sedation (21%), tachycardia (17%), constipation (16%), dizziness (14%), hypersalivation (13%), hypotension (13%), and fever (13%).

drugs.boxed_warning: Elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis treated with antipsychotic drugs are at an increased risk of death. Antidepressants increased the risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviors in children, adolescents, and young adults in short-term studies.
drugs.dosage_and_administration: Administer once daily without regard to meals. Dosage adjustment is required with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers.
drugs.warnings_and_cautions: Somnolence occurred in 11% of aripiprazole-treated adults versus 6% on placebo. Patients should be cautioned about operating hazardous machinery, including automobiles, until they are reasonably certain that therapy with aripiprazole does not affect them adversely.
drugs.food_effect: May be administered without regard to meals; no clinically significant food effect on absorption is specified.
drugs.drug_interactions: For patients taking strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., itraconazole, clarithromycin), administer half the usual dose. For patients taking strong CYP3A4 inducers (carbamazepine, rifampin), double the usual dose over 1 to 2 weeks.
drugs.common_adverse_reactions: Adults: headache (27%), insomnia (18%), anxiety (17%), nausea (15%), dizziness (10%), akathisia (10%). Pediatric: somnolence (16%), headache (12%), sedation (9%), tremor (9%), increased appetite (7%).

drugs.boxed_warning: Increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis treated with antipsychotic drugs, and increased risk of suicidal thoughts and behavior in children, adolescents and young adults.
drugs.dosage_and_administration: Quetiapine tablets, USP can be taken with or without food. Dose should be reduced to one sixth of the original dose with a potent CYP3A4 inhibitor, and may be increased up to 5-fold with a potent CYP3A4 inducer.
drugs.warnings_and_cautions: Somnolence was reported in 57% (398/698) of patients on quetiapine compared to 15% (51/347) of placebo patients in bipolar depression trials. Caution patients about performing activities requiring mental alertness, such as operating a motor vehicle, until they are reasonably certain that quetiapine therapy does not affect them adversely.
drugs.food_effect: Quetiapine tablets can be taken with or without food.
drugs.drug_interactions: Quetiapine dose should be reduced to one sixth of the original dose when co-medicated with a potent CYP3A4 inhibitor. Dose may be increased up to 5-fold of the original dose when used in combination with a potent CYP3A4 inducer.
drugs.common_adverse_reactions: Somnolence, dry mouth, dizziness, constipation, weakness, stomach pain, postural hypotension, and weight gain.

drugs.boxed_warning: Antidepressants increased the risk compared to placebo of suicidal thinking and behavior (suicidality) in children, adolescents, and young adults.
drugs.dosage_and_administration: 25 mg three or four times daily; dosage should begin at a low level and be increased as required. Elderly and adolescent patients: 30 to 50 mg/day in divided doses, or the total daily dosage may be given once a day.
drugs.warnings_and_cautions: Excessive consumption of alcohol in combination with nortriptyline therapy may have a potentiating effect, which may lead to the danger of increased suicidal attempts or overdosage. The drug may impair the mental and/or physical abilities required for the performance of hazardous tasks, such as operating machinery or driving.
drugs.drug_interactions: Contraindicated with MAO inhibitors. Significant interactions with quinidine, cimetidine, SSRIs, and drugs that can inhibit cytochrome P450 2D6. Concurrent alcohol use is cautioned against.
drugs.common_adverse_reactions: Dry mouth, blurred vision, constipation, urinary retention, tachycardia, dizziness, drowsiness, nausea/vomiting, and other anticholinergic effects.

drugs.boxed_warning: Antidepressants increased the risk compared to placebo of suicidal thinking and behavior in children, adolescents, and young adults in short-term studies.
drugs.dosage_and_administration: Outpatients: begin at 75 mg daily in divided doses, may increase to 150 mg per day. Hospitalized patients may require 100 mg initially, increasing to 200 mg or 300 mg daily. Elderly and adolescent patients: lower doses, 10 mg three times daily plus 20 mg at bedtime.
drugs.warnings_and_cautions: Amitriptyline may enhance the response to alcohol and the effects of barbiturates and other CNS depressants. Patients should be advised regarding possible impairment of mental and/or physical abilities required for performance of hazardous tasks, such as operating machinery or driving.
drugs.drug_interactions: MAO inhibitors are contraindicated; a 14-day washout is required. Topiramate may significantly increase amitriptyline concentration. SSRIs inhibit P450 2D6 metabolism; at least 5 weeks are necessary after fluoxetine discontinuation. Cimetidine reduces hepatic metabolism, increasing steady-state levels.
drugs.common_adverse_reactions: Anticholinergic effects (dry mouth, urinary retention, constipation, blurred vision); orthostatic hypotension, tachycardia; drowsiness, dizziness, tremors; rash, urticaria.

notes:
All 10 drugs retrieved from api.fda.gov/drug/label.json. Caveats for the lookup table:

1. ZIPRASIDONE MEAL SIZE NOT CONFIRMED. The label returned states "administer orally with food" and that absorption is "increased up to two-fold in the presence of food" (bioavailability ~60%), but the widely cited "at least 500 calories" threshold was NOT present in the retrieved label text. Do not encode a 500-kcal rule citing this URL; it derives from clinical pharmacology literature (Lincoln et al.) and needs its own citation, or a re-fetch of the Geodon NDA label section 12.3.

2. BRAND NAMES ARE PARTLY INFERRED. openFDA returned generic-manufacturer labels for phenelzine (Lupin), ziprasidone, aripiprazole, quetiapine (immediate-release), nortriptyline (Teva), amitriptyline, clozapine (Mylan ODT) with no proprietary name in the document. Nardil, Geodon, Abilify, Seroquel, Pamelor, Elavil, Clozaril/FazaClo/Versacloz are well-known trade names but were not all verbatim in the fetched label — treat the brands array as informational, not label-cited. Confirmed in-document: Parnate (tranylcypromine), ZYPREXA and Symbyax (olanzapine), SEROQUEL XR (quetiapine XR).

3. LITHIUM label returned is a repackager (Hetero Labs / RemedyRepack) with no brand name; the sodium/fluid text ("maintain a normal diet, including salt, and an adequate fluid intake (2,500 to 3,000 mL)") is verbatim and is the key rule. Note the "avoid sodium restriction or diuretic administration" phrasing appears in the pregnancy context in this label.

4. QUETIAPINE ALCOHOL: the retrieved label did not surface explicit alcohol-interaction text; the sedation/driving text is confirmed. Alcohol avoidance for quetiapine should be sourced separately before being asserted as label-derived.

5. CLOZAPINE food effect field left empty — no food-effect statement was extracted; the clozapine ODT dosing is CYP1A2/3A4-driven, not food-driven. Also note the retrieved clozapine label is the ODT formulation, so dosing text is ODT-specific.

6. Excerpts were trimmed to the character limits and lightly joined where the source split a rule across bullets; each remains a faithful clinical statement, but for a citation-strict prototype I recommend a verification pass that re-pulls each field directly from the JSON array (not via a summarizing fetch) so stored text is byte-exact to the label. The summarization layer used here is the main fidelity risk in this dataset.
